title: Maintenance manual
what: It counts the print hours of every printer and tells you when a maintenance task is due. The hours come from the server's print history; the value the printer shows is typed in once, and from then on both counters move with every print.
counters: Every printer carries two figures, and they are kept in step:
countersStep1: Server hours: everything this server has printed since the printer was set up.
countersStep2: Display value: the number on the printer. Type it in once. On my printer it read 14d 7h; written as 343 h it is the same figure, and the module reads both the same way.
countersStep3: From then on both move with every finished print. When they drift apart, correct the display value again.
sets: A set is a named plan with several lines: a task, an interval, optionally a material. Every printer follows exactly one set.
setsShipped: Eight sets ship with the module: seven for a model (Core One, Core One L, HT90, XL, MK4S, MK3, M3) and one for any printer. Each names the Prusa Knowledge Base article it came from.
setsCopy: A shipped set cannot be edited or deleted. Duplicate it, change the copy, assign that one.
setsAssign: Assign it on the printer's tab, in the Schedule field. The printer keeps its own hours and its Done marks; only the lines around them change.
setsOff: Switching one off works too: it leaves the list but stays in the module.
intervals: A line counts either in print hours or in days. Hours suit parts that wear with use. Days suit a calendar check, such as the linear rail once a quarter, even when the printer runs little. Done asks first and anchors the next interval at the printer's current hours.
nozzles: A nozzle line chooses its material, and the interval follows the life of that material:
tools: Each printer's tab also shows how many hours ran through every tool. The module reads the G-code of finished prints, .gcode and .bgcode, deflate, heatshrink and MeatPack included, and splits the print's length by the filament each tool pushed. The figure is an indication, not a measurement, and the tab says so. After a nozzle change, Start over at 0 resets that tool alone; the printer's counter stays where it is. Time is kept to the second: on an INDX print a nozzle sometimes works for forty seconds, and counted in whole minutes that would look as if nothing had been recorded at all. That sounds like pedantry, but it isn't - well, a little.
status: Every task carries a state, and the state follows the share of its interval that is used. The state decides two things: the dot before the task and where the task sits in its printer's list.
card: Maintenance due lists each printer's tasks with a coloured dot and the share used. Red first, then yellow, then green; a printer without a name shows its model. A printer that is all green still gets its group - a green line is the proof that this interval holds.
where: The shipped sets come from the Prusa Knowledge Base, each line linking its article, and the nozzle lives are from there too. When in doubt, check a number at the source instead of trusting the module.
check1: No counter moves: is the printer the same one the server knows? A printer set up anew starts at zero.
check2: Tool hours are missing: the G-code has to sit in the server's storage as a finished print, and the module needs read_storage.
check3: Everything green although you printed: display value and server hours apart? Type the display value in again.
captionTab: The Maintenance tab of a printer: the counter, the hours this server saw, the tool hours and every task with its state.
captionSchedules: The Maintenance page holds the schedules. A shipped one can be switched off or duplicated, never edited.
captionSchedulePicker: The Schedule field on a printer picks the plan it follows. Its own hours and Done marks stay.
captionTasks: Tasks of a shipped schedule, with the nozzle material chosen per line and the interval it brings.
captionGallery: Add a card from the gallery: one Maintenance card exists, and its settings decide what it shows.
captionSettings: The card's setting: all printers, or one from the fleet. One card per printer works this way too.
captionDashboard: Two cards on one dashboard, one for the fleet and one for a single printer.
statusOkBody: enough time. The share used is below the threshold, and the task sits at the bottom of its group.
statusSoonBody: the threshold is reached, 90 percent of the interval by default. Plan it, no need to panic. It moves above the green lines of its group.
statusDueBody: the interval is over, past 100 percent. The task sits at the top of its group, and the module publishes an event on the bus.
language: The language of the extension is set on the server, not here: Extensions, Maintenance, Settings, the field language. There, system means the language the browser asks for, and en, de or cs pin one. Czech is cs, not cz, though a country code is accepted as a courtesy.
languageRestart: The choice is stored at once and read at start-up, so the module restarts when it is saved. Pick a quiet moment: an import halfway through, or a print whose G-code is being read, is cut off by that restart. A language this package does not carry falls back to the browser's, and from there to English. The buttons above switch the language for this visit without saving anything.
languageContribute: Want your own language? Then help on GitHub. Copy locales/en.json and manual/en.json to <tag>.json, translate the values, keep the keys, open a pull request. Nobody here should write a language they do not speak, and a machine translation reads like one. The Czech is exactly that: a trial balloon, translated by a machine. Whether it holds up is for Czech readers to say.
captionLanguage: The language field in the server's settings for this extension, with the value system and the description beside it.
